text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The head of Vilnius police, Vytautas Leipus, resigned after a second diplomat was attacked in the capital on Sunday. Patrick Donabedian, a cultural attache in the French embassy, was badly beaten and robbed on Sunday afternoon.
- The chairman of the bankrupt Tauras bank Gintaras Terleckas and his deputy Rasa Sherieniene, suspected of squandering 2.5 million litas, were put in prison on Monday.
- A lorry carrying 4.4 tonnes of Regapol powder mixed with radioactive tori 232-228 was detained at the Lithuanian- Belarus border on Friday night. The load released 300 microroentgens per hour.
Regapol powder is used in the optics industry. The load belongs to an Irish firm and was being transported as production waste.
- Kalnapilis brewery posted 14.1 million litas net profit for the first half of 1997, 4 million litas more than its profit for all of 1996.
- The shareholders of Utenos Beverages rejected the offer of Denmark's Carlsberg on Monday and voted to establish a joint company with Baltic Beverages Holding.
- British flight precision experts said that Siauliu airport meets ICAO standards and the certificate is expected before the end of August.
- The chairman of NATO military committee general Klaus Nauman starts his two-day visit to Lithuania today.
- Lithuania will offer its oppinion on the conclusions of European Comission to the foreign ministers of the EU who meet in Luxembourg today.
- The general shareholdres' meeting of Ukio Bank on Tuesday will offer to increase the number of its council members to 11 from nine.
- Interrior ministry started a case against the chairman of Litimpeks Bank, Gintautas Preidys, who is suspected of misapropriating the bank's funds.
- The Labour Inspection inspected 1,085 companies in June and discovered 1874 violations.
- The state budget has collected 2.782 billion litas in revenues during the first half of 1997, 62 million litas more than planned.
